subject: math
cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
intro: Each problem gives you a scale written as $1 : n$ and one length. Multiply by $n$ to go from a drawing length to the actual length, and divide by $n$ to go from an actual length to a drawing length. The two units are already compatible, so no unit conversion is needed.

items.prompt: A map uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 6\text{ km}$. Two towns are $5\text{ cm}$ apart on the map. What is the actual distance between the towns?

steps: Each $1\text{ cm}$ on the map represents $6\text{ km}$ in reality, so multiply the map length by $6$.
The actual distance is $30\text{ km}$.

items.prompt: A blueprint uses the scale $1\text{ in} : 4\text{ ft}$. A hallway is $7\text{ in}$ long on the blueprint. How long is the actual hallway?

steps: Each $1\text{ in}$ on the blueprint represents $4\text{ ft}$, so multiply by $4$.
The actual hallway is $28\text{ ft}$ long.

items.prompt: A drawing uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 3\text{ m}$. A wall is drawn $8\text{ cm}$ long. What is the actual length of the wall?

steps: Each $1\text{ cm}$ in the drawing stands for $3\text{ m}$, so multiply by $3$.
The actual wall is $24\text{ m}$ long.

items.prompt: A model plan uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 2\text{ m}$. A room is drawn $9\text{ cm}$ wide. How wide is the actual room?

steps: Each $1\text{ cm}$ represents $2\text{ m}$, so multiply the drawing width by $2$.
The actual room is $18\text{ m}$ wide.

items.prompt: A map uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 10\text{ km}$. A river is $6\text{ cm}$ long on the map. What is the actual length of the river?

steps: Each $1\text{ cm}$ on the map represents $10\text{ km}$, so multiply by $10$.
The actual river is $60\text{ km}$ long.

items.prompt: A blueprint uses the scale $1\text{ ft} : 5\text{ ft}$. A beam is $4\text{ ft}$ long on the blueprint. How long is the actual beam?

steps: Each $1\text{ ft}$ on the blueprint represents $5\text{ ft}$ in reality, so multiply by $5$.
The actual beam is $20\text{ ft}$ long.

items.prompt: A scale drawing uses $1\text{ cm} : 7\text{ m}$. A fence is drawn $3\text{ cm}$ long. What is the actual length of the fence?

steps: Each $1\text{ cm}$ stands for $7\text{ m}$, so multiply by $7$.
The actual fence is $21\text{ m}$ long.

items.prompt: A blueprint uses the scale $1\text{ in} : 3\text{ ft}$. A bookshelf is $9\text{ ft}$ tall in real life. How tall is it on the blueprint?

steps: Each $3\text{ ft}$ of actual height equals $1\text{ in}$ on the blueprint, so divide the actual height by $3$.
On the blueprint the bookshelf is $3\text{ in}$ tall.

items.prompt: A map uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ km}$. A trail is $40\text{ km}$ long in real life. How long is the trail on the map?

steps: Each $5\text{ km}$ of actual distance equals $1\text{ cm}$ on the map, so divide the actual length by $5$.
On the map the trail is $8\text{ cm}$ long.

items.prompt: A drawing uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 4\text{ m}$. A garden path is $24\text{ m}$ long in real life. How long is it in the drawing?

steps: Each $4\text{ m}$ of actual length equals $1\text{ cm}$ in the drawing, so divide by $4$.
In the drawing the path is $6\text{ cm}$ long.

items.prompt: A blueprint uses the scale $1\text{ in} : 2\text{ ft}$. A door is $7\text{ ft}$ tall in real life. How tall is the door on the blueprint?

steps: Each $2\text{ ft}$ of actual height equals $1\text{ in}$ on the blueprint, so divide by $2$.
On the blueprint the door is $3.5\text{ in}$ tall.

items.prompt: A map uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 8\text{ km}$. A road is $4\text{ cm}$ long on the map. What is the actual length of the road?

steps: Each $1\text{ cm}$ on the map represents $8\text{ km}$, so multiply by $8$.
The actual road is $32\text{ km}$ long.

items.prompt: A scale drawing uses $1\text{ m} : 9\text{ m}$. A pool is $5\text{ m}$ long in the drawing. How long is the actual pool?

steps: Each $1\text{ m}$ in the drawing represents $9\text{ m}$ in reality, so multiply by $9$.
The actual pool is $45\text{ m}$ long.

items.prompt: A blueprint uses the scale $1\text{ in} : 6\text{ ft}$. A countertop is $42\text{ ft}$ long in real life. How long is it on the blueprint?

steps: Each $6\text{ ft}$ of actual length equals $1\text{ in}$ on the blueprint, so divide by $6$.
On the blueprint the countertop is $7\text{ in}$ long.

items.prompt: A drawing uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 3\text{ km}$. A bike route is $27\text{ km}$ long in real life. How long is it in the drawing?

steps: Each $3\text{ km}$ of actual distance equals $1\text{ cm}$ in the drawing, so divide by $3$.
In the drawing the route is $9\text{ cm}$ long.
